# Vulpkanin
Vulpkanin are a species of large, bipedal canines, they posses a thick coating of fur that covers their whole body as well as a bushy, fox-like tail.
## Racial Features - They [color=#1e90ff]can safely eat raw meat[/color] but are [color=#ffa500]poisoned by theobromine[/color]. - They get hungry and thirsty [color=#ffa500]50% faster[/color] but can metabolise chemicals [color=#1e90ff]25% faster[/color]. - Their blood is sulfur based and has a distinct yellow color. - Thanks to their claws they deal [color=red]3[/color] slash damage and [color=red]2[/color] pierce damage with their unarmed attacks. - Due to their thick fur, they take [color=#ffa500]15% more heat damage.[/color] and [color=#1e90ff]15% less cold damage[/color]. - Additionally, they cool down 70% slower and heat up 20% faster. - Their standard body heat is 37 degrees Celcius and they [color=#1e90ff]can withstand temperatures between -45 and 50 degrees Celcius[/color]. - They take [color=#1e90ff]50% less cold damage from freezing[/color] and [color=#ffa500]15% more damage from overheating[/color]. - They can see roughly [color=#1e90ff]1 tile further[/color].
## Canilunzt The Vulpkanin language, known as Canilunzt, is composed of a series of grunts, barks, yips and howls as well as several tail and ear movements that Vulpkanin do instinctually. It is often described as very harsh on the throat and difficult to learn for species that lack ears or tails. Thanks to this instinctual understanding of tail and ear movements, Vulpkanin are capable of understanding most dogs and foxes.
## Age and Names Vulpkanin are a somewhat shorter lived species, reaching adulthood at around 10 years of age and being capable to live up to 120 years. Their names are often given to them by their parents upon birth, following a naming scheme that has been described as "Germanic" by humans.
